title: 12.2 p-Circuits: Neither Digital Nor Analog
problem: Traditional analog and digital circuits present inherent trade-offs in power, area, and performance; a new computing paradigm is needed that combines benefits of both without requiring ADC/DAC conversions.
motivation: Custom ASICs demand ultra-high efficiency; a computational model bridging analog and digital without conversion overhead could enable new optimization opportunities.
method: p-circuits avoid the power and area costs of converting between analog and digital by using a hybrid approach: inputs and outputs look digital, but the actual computation happens through probability. Each output is a random 0 or 1, where how often it outputs 1 (versus 0) is controlled by an analog function that smoothly responds to the inputs. By manipulating these probabilities, the circuit performs calculations without ever converting signals between analog and digital domains.
key_novelty: p-circuits use probability as the fundamental computational substrate, with analog functions directly controlling output probabilities instead of requiring costly digital-analog conversions.
contributions: New p-circuit computational paradigm combining digital interfaces with analog probability functions
Elimination of ADC/DAC overhead in circuits requiring probabilistic computation
Unified framework for hybrid analog-digital processing
primary_theme: Probabilistic circuits bridging analog and digital computation
